# Create SRS Workflow (TTS variant — in-depth business specification)

**Goal:** Produce a deep, audit-grade SRS (`srs.md`) for an existing story FOLDER, going beyond the stub generated by `bmad-tts-create-story`. The SRS is the **source of truth for business behavior** — the document QA/PM/Dev all reference when arguing about what the system must do.

**Your Role:** Business analyst + test architect. You translate raw requirements into unambiguous BDD scenarios, surface edge cases the team would otherwise discover in production, and call out genuine ambiguities for the PM to resolve.

- Communicate all responses in {communication_language}; generate document content in {document_output_language}.
- Your input is `story.md` (mandatory); cross-reference PRD, architecture, epics, UX upstream to enrich.
- Edge-case discovery is non-negotiable — apply the systematic checklist in `references/scenario-patterns.md`.
- When upstream context is genuinely missing, mark `[CẦN BỔ SUNG: <one-line reason>]`. Never fabricate business rules.
- Open ambiguities are surfaced explicitly in the "Câu hỏi mở" section so PM can resolve before dev starts.

## Conventions

- Bare paths (e.g. `assets/srs-template.md`) resolve from the skill root.
- `{skill-root}` resolves to this skill's installed directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- `{skill-name}` resolves to `bmad-tts-create-srs`.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Resolve the Workflow Block

Run: `python3 {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --key workflow`

If the script fails, resolve the `workflow` block yourself by reading these three files in base → team → user order and applying structural merge rules: `{skill-root}/customize.toml`, `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.toml`, `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/{skill-name}.user.toml`. Scalars override, tables deep-merge, arrays of tables keyed by `code`/`id` replace matching entries and append new ones, all other arrays append.

### Step 2: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each entry in `{workflow.activation_steps_prepend}` in order before proceeding.

### Step 3: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry in `{workflow.persistent_facts}` as foundational context for the whole run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs — load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim.

### Step 4: Parse Arguments & Detect Headless

- `--story <path>` — explicit story.md path; skip auto-discovery.
- `--story-key <key>` — story key like `1-2-user-auth`; resolve to `{implementation_artifacts}/{key}/story.md`.
- `--headless` / `-H` — non-interactive; default all decisions to safe values, halt only on missing mandatory input.

Set `{headless_mode}` accordingly.

### Step 5: Load Config

Load available config from `{project-root}/_bmad/config.toml` and `{project-root}/_bmad/config.user.toml` (root and `[modules.bmm]` section), or fall back to `{project-root}/_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` if TOML missing. Resolve:

- `project_name`, `user_name`
- `communication_language`, `document_output_language`
- `planning_artifacts`, `implementation_artifacts`
- `date` = system-generated current datetime

If config is missing, inform the user that `bmad-bmb-setup` (or the appropriate setup skill) can configure the project, then continue with sensible defaults.

### Step 6: Greet the User

Greet `{user_name}` in `{communication_language}`. Skip greet if `{headless_mode}` is true.

### Step 7: Execute Append Steps

Execute each entry in `{workflow.activation_steps_append}` in order.

Activation complete. Begin the workflow below.

## Paths

- `sprint_status` = `{implementation_artifacts}/sprint-status.yaml`
- `epics_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/epics.md`
- `prd_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/prd.md`
- `architecture_file` = `{planning_artifacts}/architecture.md`
- `ux_file_pattern` = `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*.md`
- `story_dir` = `{implementation_artifacts}/{{story_key}}/`
- `story_file` = `{story_dir}/story.md`
- `detail_design_file` = `{story_dir}/detail-design.md`
- `srs_output_path` = `{workflow.srs_output_path}`  (defaults to `{story_dir}/srs.md`)
- `srs_template` = `{workflow.srs_template}`  (defaults to `assets/srs-template.md`)

## Input Files

| Input | Description | Path Pattern(s) | Load Strategy |
|-------|-------------|------------------|---------------|
| story | **MANDATORY** — story document produced by `bmad-tts-create-story` | `{story_dir}/story.md` | FULL_LOAD |
| detail-design | Technical design (helps map scenarios to system surfaces) | `{story_dir}/detail-design.md` | FULL_LOAD if exists |
| epics | Epic with original ACs + business value | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*epic*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*epic*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD by epic_num |
| prd | Product requirements (NFR, business rules, scope) | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*prd*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |
| architecture | Architecture (integration points, system boundaries — informs scenario surface) | whole: `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*.md`, sharded: `{planning_artifacts}/*architecture*/*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |
| ux | UX flows (informs user-facing scenarios) | `{planning_artifacts}/*ux*.md` | SELECTIVE_LOAD |

## Execution

<workflow>

<step n="1" goal="Resolve target story and load context exhaustively">

<check if="--story arg provided">
  <action>Use the path verbatim. Derive `{{story_dir}}` = parent dir of story file. Parse `{{epic_num}}`, `{{story_num}}`, `{{story_key}}`, `{{story_title}}` from story_dir basename or from inside story.md frontmatter/heading.</action>
</check>

<check if="--story-key arg provided">
  <action>Set `{{story_key}}` from arg. Set `{{story_dir}}` = `{implementation_artifacts}/{{story_key}}/`. Parse `{{epic_num}}`, `{{story_num}}`, `{{story_title}}` from key.</action>
</check>

<check if="no story arg AND not headless">
  <action>Auto-discover from `{sprint_status}`: find the most recent story whose status is `ready-for-dev`, `designed`, or `in-progress` (i.e. the story that just had `tts-create-story` run). If multiple candidates, ask the user to choose. If none, ask user to provide story-key or path.</action>
</check>

<check if="headless AND no story arg">
  <action>HALT with: "Headless mode requires --story <path> or --story-key <key>."</action>
</check>

<critical>Verify `{{story_file}}` exists. If missing, HALT with: "story.md không tồn tại tại {{story_file}}. Hãy chạy `/bmad-tts-create-story` trước."</critical>

<action>Load these in parallel — exhaustively, do not skim:
  - `{{story_file}}` (full): user story, ACs, dev notes, acceptance criteria, references
  - `{detail_design_file}` if exists: technical surfaces, data flows, integration points
  - Epic for this story from epics file: epic objectives, business value, full AC list, source hints
  - PRD: NFR section, business rules, scope/non-goals, glossary
  - Architecture: integration points, security/auth model, data contracts, error semantics — focus on surfaces this story touches
  - UX: user flows, error states, role-specific flows
  - Persistent facts loaded during activation (project-context.md)
</action>

<action>Cross-reference: for each AC in story.md, locate its corresponding epic AC (verbatim) and any related PRD/architecture passages. Note discrepancies — if story.md ACs differ from epic ACs, flag for the "Câu hỏi mở" section.</action>

</step>

<step n="2" goal="Synthesize SRS — apply scenario discipline">

<critical>Load `references/scenario-patterns.md` and apply the edge-case checklist systematically. Skipping this step is the difference between a stub SRS and an audit-grade one.</critical>

<action>For each AC, derive scenarios:
  - **Happy path** — minimum 1 scenario per AC; use Given/When/Then with concrete data.
  - **Edge cases** — apply checklist (boundary, concurrency, network/auth failure, data corruption, role mismatch, idempotency, retry, race conditions). Add scenarios only when the story's domain genuinely involves that dimension; do not pad.
  - **Error path** — explicit error scenarios with error codes, user-facing messages, recovery behavior.
</action>

<action>Number scenarios `H1, H2, ...` (happy), `E1, E2, ...` (edge), `R1, R2, ...` (error/recovery). Each scenario MUST reference one or more `AC-N`.</action>

<action>Extract business rules (`BR-N`) — invariants the system must always uphold. Sources: PRD constraints, epic non-goals, architecture security/data rules, project-context. If no explicit rules, mark `[CẦN BỔ SUNG: ...]` rather than inventing.</action>

<action>Identify pre/post-conditions per scenario family. State data, auth state, feature flags, prerequisite stories.</action>

<action>Curate test data examples — concrete sample inputs/outputs that QA can paste directly. Cover: valid baseline, boundary values, malformed inputs, role variants. Use realistic Vietnamese-context data where applicable (tên, địa chỉ, số CMND format, ...).</action>

<action>Extract NFRs from PRD (performance, security, accessibility, i18n). If story has no story-specific NFR, write "Tuân theo NFR mặc định của hệ thống" — do not pad.</action>

<action>Build "Câu hỏi mở" (open questions) — ambiguities that block confident implementation. Sources:
  - Conflicts between story.md ACs and epic ACs
  - Missing NFR for behaviors that need them (e.g. timeout, retry policy)
  - Edge cases the original AC doesn't address
  - Stakeholder/role boundaries that aren't defined
  Each question is one line, addressed to a role (PM/SA/UX/QA).
</action>

</step>

<step n="3" goal="Write srs.md from template">

<action>Load template from `{srs_template}`. If template path is bare, resolve from `{skill-root}`.</action>

<action>Render the template by replacing every `{{srs_*}}` placeholder. Filling rules:
  - All prose in `{document_output_language}`.
  - Preserve all headings exactly. Never delete a section — if empty, leave `[CẦN BỔ SUNG: <reason>]`.
  - Tables: use markdown table syntax.
  - Scenarios: use the canonical Given/When/Then bullet format (see template comments for exemplar).
  - AC numbering: `AC-1`, `AC-2`, ... preserving original BDD wording verbatim from epic.
  - BR numbering: `BR-1`, `BR-2`, ...
  - Scenario IDs: `H1, E1, R1, ...` with AC refs.
</action>

<action>Save to `{srs_output_path}`. If a file exists at that path (typically the stub created by `tts-create-story`), overwrite unconditionally.</action>

</step>

<step n="4" goal="Finalize and chain">

<action>Print a structured summary in {communication_language}:
  - Path saved (`{srs_output_path}`)
  - Counts: ACs, scenarios (H/E/R), business rules, open questions
  - Top 3 most important open questions to resolve before dev starts
  - Any `[CẦN BỔ SUNG: ...]` markers grouped by section
</action>

<action>If `{workflow.on_complete}` is non-empty, execute it as a chained instruction. Pass through `{{story_file}}`, `{{story_key}}`, `{{story_dir}}`, and `{headless_mode}` (as `--headless` flag) where the chained skill needs them.</action>

</step>

</workflow>
